title: Efficiently map a column id to it's value in pySpark
question:
I working with pyspark for the first time and getting used to distributed computing. I've been able to tweak things to run well for most of my use cases, but have one I seem to have a big performance hit on. I'm trying to map ID I have on my large df with values that come from a much smaller mapping table ex (1 = USA, 2 = Canada, 3 = France, ....)

I have this mapping table in a dictionary and then use spark F.createmap which I apply using a select onto the entire large df. I have about 50 or so of these mappings to apply so it slows down my processing quite a bit. Given that most of these mapping tables are tiny (often 5-50 rows) is there a more efficient solution I could explore?

Here is what I tried so far:

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

# Initialize Spark session
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("MyMappingIssue").getOrCreate()

# Sample data for the large DataFrame
data = [(1, 'other_data1'), (2, 'other_data2'), (3, 'other_data3')]
columns = ["countryid", "other_column"]
df = spark.createDataFrame(data, columns)


mapping_dict = {1: 'USA', 2: 'Canada', 3: 'France'}

mapping_expr = F.create_map([F.lit(x) for x in chain(*mapping_dict.item())])

mapped_df = df.select(
    *,
    mapping_exp[col("countryid")].alias("country_name")
)
answer:
i could think of 2 options and you should, ideally, test those on your data to understand which one works best for your data use case.

Option 1

create a dataframe using the mapping_dict and do a left join

mapping_sdf = spark.createDataFrame(mapping_dict.items(), ['countryid', 'country'])

# +---------+-------+
# |countryid|country|
# +---------+-------+
# |        1|    USA|
# |        2| Canada|
# |        3| France|
# +---------+-------+

data_sdf. \
    join(func.broadcast(mapping_sdf), 'countryid', 'left'). \
    drop('countryid'). \
    show()

# +------------+-------+
# |other_column|country|
# +------------+-------+
# | other_data1|    USA|
# | other_data3| France|
# | other_data2| Canada|
# +------------+-------+

Option 2

create dynamic case when statement using the mapping_dict items

case_whens = reduce(lambda x, y: x.when(func.col('countryid') == y[0], y[1]), mapping_dict.items(), func)
# Column<'CASE WHEN (countryid = 1) THEN USA WHEN (countryid = 2) THEN Canada WHEN (countryid = 3) THEN France END'>

data_sdf. \
    withColumn('country', case_whens). \
    drop('countryid'). \
    show()

# +------------+-------+
# |other_column|country|
# +------------+-------+
# | other_data1|    USA|
# | other_data2| Canada|
# | other_data3| France|
# +------------+-------+
